hook_text: Bloemfontein, Matjiesfontein, Koffiefontein. Why do so many South African town names include the word for a spring?
clip_script: The Vaal River at Vereeniging. Water for drinking, farming and factories. All over South Africa, settlements grew where nature helped: next to rivers and springs, on flat land with fertile soil, in places with enough rain, near grasslands for cattle, at sheltered bays for harbours and at the foot of mountain passes. Even town names tell the story: fontein means spring, drift means a place to cross a river, and port means a harbour.
visual_style: Whiteboard map of South Africa with towns popping up beside rivers, springs and bays, and labels showing fontein, drift and port in town names.
mood: Curious and detective-like, like solving the mystery of a map.
pacing: One natural reason at a time, each with a South African town as a clue.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find three town names on a map that tell you about a natural feature.
